definitions.explanation: A book used alongside the main textbook in school education to provide additional material or different perspectives on a subject. Often produced by local governments or educational boards.

examples.japanese: {副読本|ふくどくほん}を{配布|はいふ}する。
{道徳|どうとく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{副読本|ふくどくほん}を{使|つか}った。
examples.english: We used a supplementary reader in the moral education class.

examples.japanese: {市|し}が{作成|さくせい}した{防災|ぼうさい}の{副読本|ふくどくほん}が{全校|ぜんこう}に{配|くば}られた。
examples.english: A disaster-preparedness supplementary reader created by the city was distributed to all schools.

notes: Commonly used in Japanese elementary and junior high school education. {副読本|ふくどくほん} are often produced for subjects like moral education ({道徳|どうとく}), local studies ({郷土|きょうど}{学習|がくしゅう}), and disaster preparedness ({防災|ぼうさい}). Unlike the main textbook ({教科書|きょうかしょ}), they do not require Ministry of Education approval and are often created by municipalities.
